headline: Florida Republicans who strongly oppose AI have criticised OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman's comments that the world should accept some bad things from AI.
score_reason: Lowered by 1 from the pool score of 5: only the headline was available, so who spoke and what was said are unverified.
importance_line: Altman's remark is drawing political fire in Florida, whose attorney general is already suing OpenAI over ChatGPT according to The Capitolist, which affects Floridians and AI firms, but who spoke and what they plan to do are not yet known.
summary: Politico reports that Florida Republicans who are among the firmest opponents of AI have criticised OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman's remark, in the Politico interview we reported on 5 Oct, that the world should accept "some bad things happening".
notes: Politico's page returned 403 and no other outlet carries the story, so the entry rests on the headline only. Reply to Altman's remark in the Politico Decoded interview (our 5 Oct edition item 96); pool flags it as a follow-up of 1005:C05-01. The page address contains 'uthmeier-ag' (apparently Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier) but the headline names no one, so the entry does not. The headline quotes 'That is recklessness' without naming the speaker. Background in the importance line is from The Capitolist (Uthmeier sued OpenAI and Altman over ChatGPT; on 28 Sep he asked a court for a temporary injunction).
